reaction.class: carbamate (urethane) bond hydrolysis at an aliphatic nitrogen

substrate.physical_state: water-soluble small-molecule biscarbamate in which the two carbamate nitrogens are joined by a flexible saturated six-carbon chain and each carbamate oxygen carries a short oligo-ether alcohol chain
substrate.access_constraint: candidate must be assessed for its ability to cleave a resonance-stabilised linkage whose nitrogen bears no electron-withdrawing aromatic substituent, which makes the carbonyl less electrophilic and the amine a poorer leaving group than in the aryl-substituted case
substrate.product_context: full cleavage of both linkages releases a free flexible aliphatic diamine, the free oligo-ether alcohol, and carbon dioxide

enzyme_requirements.nucleophile: possess a catalytic nucleophile capable of attacking a carbamate carbonyl that is deactivated relative to both an ester and an aryl-substituted carbamate
enzyme_requirements.leaving_group: accommodate alcohol departure and the subsequent breakdown of the resulting carbamic acid, without requiring an aromatic ring to stabilise the developing charge
enzyme_requirements.pocket: assess whether the substrate-binding site is an open or extended channel able to accommodate a long flexible aliphatic chain spanning the two reactive centres
enzyme_requirements.secretion_and_stability: note any evidence of extracellular localisation or elevated thermal stability, since process conditions for this substrate are harsh

review_requirements: Assess reaction direction: cleavage of the stated linkage rather than its formation or transfer to another acceptor.
Distinguish demonstrated activity on the stated substrate class from promiscuous or trace activity inferred from a surrogate reporter molecule.

Assess compatibility with a flexible saturated aliphatic substituent at the nitrogen of the scissile bond, and specifically whether evidence exists for the aliphatic case rather than being carried over from an aromatic one.
Assess whether the catalytic site is open enough to admit a long-chain substrate rather than only a compact one.
Assess whether the evidence is a purified-enzyme measurement with quantified product, or only an annotation, a homology inference, or a whole-cell or indirect observation.
Record any reported thermal stability and any reported tolerance of organic co-solvents.

For every candidate that reaches the shortlist, harvest and record every quantitative measurement reported for it: value, units, the exact substrate measured, assay temperature, pH, enzyme loading and reaction time, and the source. Search beyond the abstract, including supplementary information, where the numbers usually are.

Record each measurement's comparability: state explicitly whether two candidates were measured on the SAME substrate under comparable conditions, since numbers from different substrates, labs or assay formats cannot be ranked against each other.
Mark any candidate with no quantitative measurement as unvalidated rather than dropping it, and say what measurement would be needed.

evidence_buckets.name: long-chain or flexible aliphatic substrate context
